findings.description: The inline user policy grants full wildcard actions on ec2, s3, lambda and cloudwatch against Resource "*", violating least privilege. Compromise of this user's long-lived access key would allow full control of compute, storage and serverless resources across the account, including data exfiltration from any S3 bucket and privilege escalation via lambda function creation/modification.

A permanent IAM access key is provisioned for a human/service user with broad permissions and no PGP key is supplied, so Terraform stores the secret and ses_smtp_password in plaintext in the state file. Static, non-rotating credentials paired with a wildcard policy are a prime target for credential theft.

An IAM user is created for programmatic access with an attached wildcard policy and static access key instead of using an assumable role with temporary credentials, creating a persistent high-privilege credential in the account.
